subject: Archaeology
title: The First Burials: When Death Got Meaning
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The First Burials: When Death Got Meaning.

hook.text: The oldest known deliberate burial is over 78,000 years old. A child was placed in a shallow grave in a Kenyan cave.

buildup.text: The child, named Mtoto, was about three years old. The body was carefully positioned on its side with flexed legs.

discovery.text: The grave was inside Panga ya Saidi cave. Soil analysis showed the pit was deliberately dug and the body covered.

twist.text: Neanderthals also buried their dead. Intentional burial may not be unique to Homo sapiens after all.

climax.text: Deliberate burial implies belief in something beyond death — or at least a bond too strong to abandon a body.

punchline.text: Seventy-eight thousand years ago, someone buried a child with care.

quiz.question: Why is the burial of 'Mtoto' in Kenya significant?
options: It is the only burial found with written inscriptions
It is the oldest known deliberate human burial in Africa
It contained the earliest known grave goods made of metal
